Tribit Wireless Earbuds, Qualcomm QCC3040 Bluetooth 5.2, 4 Mics CVC 8.0 Call Noise Reduction 50H Playtime Clear Calls Volume Control True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds Earphones, FlyBuds C1 Black This is a good choice for a mid range (50-70$) earbuds that comes with a few excellent features and some drawbacks that will make you love your airpods or buds even more.

The main positives - the BT connectivity is excellent and zero loss of signal while jogging/yard work etc. Never had to repair the earbuds to my phone (Note). Battery life is as advertised and very pleasing. Fit is comfortable and no heaviness or blocked feeling.

The could-be-better - getting used to the stem controls is not that easy and has been finicky at times. Volume/bass is mediocre at best. Though some noise reduction is perceivable, it is uneven. It is IPX5 rated, means it should be able to "resist a sustained, low-pressure water jet spray".

At the advertised price, you are paying really for the battery life, BT chip, above-average noise suppression and average sound. Overall, a decent pair for using in situations where you are OK sacrificing performance (travel, yard work, jogging etc - where one could lose or step on it ).
text_fidelity_b: Tribit Wireless Earbuds, Qualcomm QCC3040 Bluetooth 5.2, 4 Mics CVC 8.0 Call Noise Reduction 50H Playtime Clear Calls Volume Control True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds Earphones, FlyBuds C1 Black

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity Just spent a week and a half in hospital. After dithering for a couple of weeks, I finally took the plunge and ordered the kindle the day before surgery. I had a small satchel (guy purse) to carry wallet, kindle and phone with me when in therapy. My arms were too weak to hold the book I had with me. Friends brought my kindle to me the 3rd day. I then read about 5 to 6 hours or more a day and night. Charging was fast and I had no issues with battery life. I charged once a day. If needed I could read while kindle was charging. I bought the 3g and wi-fi addition. Downloaded on both as hospital wi-fi quit sometimes at night. Holding a book to read had become a chore for me some years ago. Sitting at a table reading was uncomfortable, therefore I have neglected to my reading. I have downloaded Edgar A. Poe's works. I especially enjoy his comic and scientific pieces. (See high school English classes ruined Poe for you, didn't it? It did for me until I discovered his other writings.) I downloaded some other large and heavy in print books. I am angry at self for not discovering the kindle and amazon book experience before now. I own some 3,000 volumes of history, science, etc. Very little fiction, except for Poe, Shakespeare, Twain, Doyle, and their ilk interests me. I don't read popular novels at all. I was surprised at the number of books and editions available for free or almost free that covers my interests. I don't consider myself as a snob for not liking popular fiction, it just doesn't interest me. But reading is a mind expanding activity, whatever one reads. It doesn't matter what you read, just do it.
I am 77 years old new kindle reader. Thanks amazon.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity

For a month or so, these worked amazingly. They hooked up to my Note 8 with no issues. The sound quality was pretty good for such a small device; not mind-blowing, but good. Everything was inline with the product reviews I'd read online.

Unfortunately, as of this morning the left earbud has become so quiet I would call it useless. One earbud quieting has been reported by many users. I hoped I'd be one of the lucky ones who didn't run into the issue, but that's turned out not to be the case.

I am surrounded by Samsung products and I love the brand, but I've chosen to return these rather than fuss with sending them in for repairs. They shouldn't need repairs after 1 month or so of use.

For the record, I used these on my daily commute and while out and about. They never got sweaty or wet. They're not clogged up. They've never been dropped or misused. I put them on to charge and the next time I went to use them, the left earbud had quit.

I gave two stars because while they worked, they were amazing. I just wish they'd lasted longer.

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Touch Mouse I was super excited to get to try out this mouse, because I've been unhappy with my Logitech Marathon Mouse, and missed my old Microsoft mouse that seemed to be so sensitive. And the features of this mouse are super-cool. I like the "magic" scrolling wheel and the way it just knows which finger I am using to click and opens the right window. The shape is attractive and reasonably ergonomic, can be used in either hand, and I liked the tiny USB receiver and the USB extension cord that lets me make sure the receiver is within range.

But this mouse was a pain to use, because the scrolling wheel simply did not work very well. It was either too sensitive and scrolled when I didn't want it to, or it wasn't sensitive enough and I'd be scrolling and SCROLLING and nothing would happen. I also ended up closing windows unintentionally and clicking on links that I didn't mean to because the scrolly wheel flipped out just as I clicked something. When I found myself putting off working because the mouse was too annoying, I finally gave up and plugged my old one back in.

This is obviously an idea that has potential, because the mac people are just raving on their magic mouse, and the pleasure of having a sleek surface with no wheel is very nice indeed. But it needs a bit more work in the execution before it's ready for prime time.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Touch Mouse

text_fidelity_a:
myCharge PowerGear Sound Protective Portable Charging Case for Wireless Earbuds Headphones | Custom Tray Compatible with Powerbeats & Removable for Other Brands | 1400 mAh / 1A Output The MyCharge is a handy if not tiny clamshell charging case for PowerBeat headphones, though it will work for others as well.

Pros:
The case itself has an hard outer shell that feels durable and thick. I have no fears the earbuds will be well protected inside. It opens and closes easily and tightly. As much as a case can be, it’s aesthetically pleasing—a dark, slick black with a black ribbon with red stitching running down the middle (the red stitching matches the red inside). The ribbon/band does more than add a bit of style and color; it also gives it a bit more texture so it grips the surface it’s atop better.

The plastic tray inside is designed for the PoweBeats line, so the earbuds nestle snugly (but with no need to wrestle or force them in) into an indentation so they lie flat and with a mid-section to insert the connecting wires/controls into. It’s a good fit, well-designed, and I don’t feel like I’m overstressing the wires, though I wouldn’t want to leave them in that position for a long amount of time (though I tend to worry about that sort of thin more than others)

It comes with a cable. You can use any one, but you’ll want it to be very short

The port to charge the case (the battery inside the case for sticklers) is easily accessible.

An LED on the front lets you know if the case battery is getting low

Cons
I wish the port cover felt a little more durable

Mixed or Up in the Air
I haven’t had it long enough yet to check how many charges, but I’ve gotten a few without a noticeable impact on the case battery. I don’t know if their promise of a dozen-plus will bear out, but I don’t think it’ll be far off if not.

The case isn’t really tiny (You can see the dimensions above). If you’re looking for something to slip into a pocket, then this will be a con, though it will easily fit a coat pocket. It will fit cargo pockets but you’ll definitely know it’s there. On the other hand, it doesn’t take up a lot of space, it’s quite protective, and if you’re worried about losing your expensive but very small and easy to lose earbuds, putting them in a noticeable, protective case that will also charge them back up is far from the worst idea. Personally, I’m OK with the size.

As noted, the case is designed for PowerBeats, so your mileage will vary on how well it fits some other type. My other earbuds all fits in the case without an issue, just not as snugly or neatly. That isn’t a real priority for me even ignoring the fact that I have PowerBeats.

Overall, a good value for what it does I’d say.
text_fidelity_b: myCharge PowerGear Sound Protective Portable Charging Case for Wireless Earbuds Headphones | Custom Tray Compatible with Powerbeats & Removable for Other Brands | 1400 mAh / 1A Output

text_fidelity_a: Mighty Mule Wireless Driveway Alarm (FM231) At first I thought mine was faulty too.. we previously had a Mighty Mule driveway sensor that we loved and had for approximately two to three years before an ants nest took it over, plus damage from the weather killed it. So when that one went bad we went to Amazon to get the same model again because we loved the other one so much.. it arrived, we installed, and we kept getting faulty signals all hours of the day and night... to the point we would just unplug it at night. We attempted to call the customer service number and it was absolutely impossible to stay on hold for that length of time and not receive one person to talk to. I did the tech ticket online and did receive an email back after 2 days. That wasn't of much use. After a few tries my husband decided to turn the sensitivity down and bury the cable little bit deeper. I believe the manual says it needs to be around a foot when we only had at 6 to 7 inches..After digging a little deeper and turning the sensitivity down it seems to have done the trick. We also have an electric fence that was nearby we had to wonder if that was causing some issues? So far we've not had one faulty signal and it has alerted every time someone has come in and out of the driveway.. I would suggest before you give up and return this to try the same thing we did. The only reason it is not getting 5 stars is because you cannot get through to customer service and the tips they gave us were to no avail.
text_fidelity_b: Mighty Mule Wireless Driveway Alarm (FM231)

If this is your second drive, you can use diskpart to get access to the full 3 gig -- just keep in mind this will erase your entire hard drive. Use it carefully. If it's your primary, your best bet is to partition it before you install Windows. If you aren't very technical, and just need a replacement drive, you're better off picking up a 2 TB, which is the biggest Win 8 can recognize without such additional configuration.

The drive itself is perfect. It's fast. It's quiet. It's reliable--I work in IT, and I've found WD drives over all to cause the fewest problems. This one has been put through some very heavy use with no issues.

Sennheiser RS 170 Digital Wireless Headphones (Discontinued By Manufacturer) I have owned these headphones since August, 2014. They are easy to use, and the sound quality is excellent. Prior to owning them, I tried out some $20 wireless headphones from a local drugstore which did not work at all, and I also did a jury-rigged setup with a very long, trip-hazard cable linking some headphones I owned to my TiVo. Never again. Both were a disaster.

This system is absolutely wonderful for two reasons:

First, I have weird hearing issues in that when I am trying to sleep, every little sound bugs me and I seem to hear even a conversation in the next room far more clearly than I have any desire to do, but when listening to TV, I can't understand 75% of what the actors are saying without captions. Go figure. With these headphones, no more problem. All dialog is clear as a bell.

Second, I no longer have to drive my husband crazy blaring the TV in order to adequately hear the actors speaking. By the same token, if my husband is watching a program on TV that I'm not at all interested in, I don't have to be subjected to listening to that either.

It's win-win.

I will say that I was not myself techie enough to install these headphones. My husband is an IT guy and he had to do it for me. So that's one downside for the customer who struggles with techie installations. Other than that, all is great.

text_fidelity_a:
Boogie Board Jot Reusable Writing Tablet, Includes 8.5 in LCD Writing Tablet, Instant Erase, Stylus Pen, Built in Magnets & Kickstand, Pink I bought two Jot 8.5 at the same time, one from a local store, black and silver, and the other here, black and gray. The silver and black jot looks nice but it didn't work with the android app well at all. It cuts off the top portion of the scan so you couldn't read the first line. I then have to crop the image and make it bigger for it to show. The auto-scan option didn't work at all. I emailed Kent Displays and they responded right away with the following; "thank you for bringing this to our attention. We do know about the app having issues with certain colored boards and the issue is being addressed. Unfortunately I do not have a timeline as to when the app will be updated. My apologies for the inconvenience."
The black and gray Jot works much better, not perfect but better. The scans work most of the time on manual but the auto scan is still touchy. It is better to have the jot on a light surface such as paper or light countertop/desk. The app needs a lot of help! It would be good to have the option to file your scans in folders and email as a pdf. If you want to get the most out of this device I would get the black gray option and stay away from the other colors.
text_fidelity_b: Boogie Board Jot Reusable Writing Tablet, Includes 8.5 in LCD Writing Tablet, Instant Erase, Stylus Pen, Built in Magnets & Kickstand, Pink

text_fidelity_a:
Sony ZX Series Wired On-Ear Headphones with Mic, White MDR-ZX110AP I certainly didn't expect anything of audiophile quality or anything astounding. Knowing how much I'm spending is the context for the review.

It's a good pair of headphones.

They're lightweight, comfortable, the earpads stay reasonably cool, the cord is just long enough to listen to at a desk (and that's a good thing), and they sound awfully good for what I paid. They also look pretty okay. The fact that they fold flat is a nice little bonus but for a pair of utility headphones, I think these are a home run.

So as a sound engineer and a musician I would put it this way. They're not high fidelity headphones, nor do they work for performance. They won't work for reference/studio work at all. They're too flimsy to call a solid pair, but for casually listening to music while multi-tasking at home or for watching a streaming video, these do just great. I think there are a number of good headphones like this one you can get for less than $20 or so. This one is up there and I would buy it again if I needed another.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ZX Series Wired On-Ear Headphones with Mic, White MDR-ZX110AP

text_fidelity_a:
Monoprice Active Indoor/Outdoor HD6 HDTV Antenna, 50 Mile Range, Video Antenna (115953) Black Before you buy, check the Monoprice website for this item. The price may be much cheaper over there.

This is a very inexpensive, relatively low quality TV antenna. You get what you pay for. They advertise this for both indoor and outdoor use, but the mostly plastic construction will not last long outdoors in areas that get a lot of wind, ice, or bright sunlight. The attached 3 foot cable really tells you what their intended use case is. If your TV is near a window, hang the antenna in the window, plug it in, and you're done.

The advertised 50 mile range is for ideal conditions, mounting the antenna outdoors in an area where there are absolutely no obstructions between your home and the TV broadcast tower (no trees, no buildings, etc). Expect much worse range for an indoor mounting and if there are any obstructions. If you live in an area with trees etc, you should get a more sturdy antenna that can be mounted on a pole on top of your roof so it can receive a signal over the trees.

This antenna is advertised for UHF frequencies only. Most TV stations use UHF these days, but in my area there are a couple that use VHF and this antenna is not usable for those channels. If you really want VHF, I suggest getting a different antenna from this one.

Over the years, I've never had a Seagate hard drive that I felt died too quickly or had any kind of unexpected problem.

So when I was given the opportunity to test this huge Seagate drive, I was thrilled. Obviously, it's a bare hard drive, so you'll need to know how to open up your computer and connect the drive. Once I did that, the drive was immediately recognized by Windows and the drivers installed automatically. In order to make the drive show up and start working in Windows 7, I had to right-click on computer, click manage, double-click storage, double-click disk management, partition it, give it a drive letter, and format it.

This drive is built to handle 24 hour a day use as storage device attached to a network. Because I am a home user, I am not using the full capability of this drive, but for my purposes, having a huge hard drive to store my collection of horticultural images in raw format, this drive is faster than my other (non-solid-state) drive and I'm not noticing any noise when the data is being accessed.

Overall, this is a huge amount of storage space for the price and would make a great drive for home user or small business user. While you'll probably want a superfast solid-state drive to run Windows and other primary programs, I use a regular drive like this for storage on my computer so that I don't need to buy a 3 TB solid-state drive (do they even make those?).

Wicked HD CARDVR1080PWHD4GB 1080p Car Camera & DVR Box (Black) UPDATE 7/13/2017: This dash cam fell off the mount yesterday. I examined it and found the plastic on the top had cracked. This is the ORIGINAL dash cam which still functions well. I am not using the more recent dash cam that Amcrest refused to update (see below for the 4/18/2017 update). Too bad it could not have been manufactured with a metal top or outer casing that would stand up to removing and replacing and repositioning.

The most recent comments (UPDATES) apply to the more recently bought WICKEDHD dash cam that carries the name AMCREST on the box.

UPDATE 4/18/2017 - When I emailed AMCREST about the problems with the camera, I was told on April 11 "Thank you for contacting Amcrest Support, my name is Kirby and I'm the Product Support Specialist here and I will do my best to assist you with any issues or questions you may be having.

We are currently working on an updated for this device. I am very sorry for the inconvenience. I will put your ticket on hold so that I can do a follow up."

Today, 4/18/2017, however, I received this from the same AMCREST person.
"Unfortunately, we no longer service this product. It has been discontinued. I am very sorry for the inconvenience."

So they waited until the 30-day return limit passed before telling me the product is discontinued. Now I am stuck with a dash cam that has to have the date set every time it is powered.

Because of this treatment / experience, I will not be buying any more AMCREST products.

UPDATE 4/9/2017 - Bought another camera, expected it to function as the first one.
HOWEVER, several problems have reared their ugly heads.
1. The date resets to 01/01/2014 whenever it is turned OFF.
2. Recording does not start when the ignition is turned on and power is supplied to the camera. The green light on the plug-in to the DC outlet is ON but the camera will not turn on.
3. Recording of video clips appear to be in one folder; they are not in folders based on the date as they were on previous cameras.

Comments below apply to the older version(s) of the WICKED HD dash cam. I gave those 4 STARS.

UPDATE 11/1/2015 - No problems except for a few stray spots that are on the sensor or the inner lens. A couple of times one 3-minute video was skipped as the recording went from one folder to another on the same uninterrupted trip. The original micro-SD card has remained in the dash cam all these months.
The camera setting is for 1080p video so that license tags in front of me and gas prices and other signs on the sides of the road will be discernible when viewed on my computer. If my vehicle is stopped for a light, the zoom produces images that are clear enough but it is obvious they are pixelated.

UPDATE 3/9/2015 - The company sent me a replacement that arrived today. Unfortunately, the box contains no rearview mirror mount for the dash cam. That will cost me another $10 to order separately.
The good news is that the micro-SD card stayed in - finally - when I inserted it into the memory card slot. That needs to be redesigned such that the mechanism doesn't eject the card as easily as it does. The cut-out doesn't match the lip on the SD card - it's on the opposite side of where it logically should be. The 'manual' simply says the micro SD card should be inserted as in the [non-existant] "image below; press it until you hear a click." No image and no click. The micro SD card doesn't stay in until just the right position is achieved.

After I have used it, I will post any comments as to the images produced. Hopefully the videos won't have the smears / streaks / spots that the first dash cam had.

UPDATE 3/3/2015 - The company sent me Return Authorization, and I spent $14 (about 25% of the cost of the dash cam - so much for Prime membership) to return the dash cam plus all attachments to them for a replacement. Attaching that mount to the rear-view mirror was not easy, so I don't look forward to having to reattach it. However, I really hope the replacement will come quickly, have a functioning micro SD card slot and not have a defective lens or sensor (streaks).

UPDATE 3/1/2015 - Through Amazon I have requested a replacement dash cam since I am unable to insert a micro SD card fully into the slot, making the dash cam unusable. The Amazon description states that this dash cam has a one-year warranty.

Original review follows- from October 23, 2014, after I had it for about 2 weeks.
This works. However, the instructions only explain what options are available via the cam's menus. They do not explain HOW to use it.

The microSD - NOT mini-SD as others have mentioned - card will not stay in the camera by pushing it with my finger. I have to use a hard object. That's no longer a problem since I discovered how to transfer images to my computer - the instructions are not there in the booklet. (Plug in the USB cable that connects the dash cam to the computer, the dash cam turns on, and press the REC button - Image Capture utility pops up on my Mac computer.)

When I used the default settings - 720 and 60 fps - and I initially set it on my GPS platform on my dash, I got video that was upside down - but clear. Now I have it attached to the rearview mirror stem.

Unfortunately, the zoom is digital, not optical, resulting in extremely pixelated video. I was unable to read license tags or other details along the road (e.g., gas station prices).

The attachment to the mirror requires two hands and standing on my head to see where the cam attaches to the mount. And then, I have to be able to attach it without having the power cable disconnect. Also, I have to double check to ensure it is aimed properly.

It goes without saying that the cam has to be removed and hidden away when parking in a public place.

The fact that it comes on when the vehicle starts is nice. I have remote start, but the cam doesn't turn on until I unlock the door and insert the key and turn the ignition switch to its running position.

Considering the price, it is a good buy (especially compared to the GoPro cams). I may use it whenever I drive somewhere, but I may have to use 1080 resolution to read license tags of those idiots on the road who don't know how to drive.

UPDATE: Today (October 28, 2014) I used 1080p resolution. Now I was able to read the license tags of the vehicles that were not too far in front of me. Also, I was able to read signs on the sides of the road. The size of each 3-minute clip is about 290 MB. That's room for about 110 clips, each of which is 3 minutes long. Using longer clips is not advisable since each clip would be a large file. I see NO gap between one clip and the next.

One problem: Each and every video has a 'smear' which is either on the inside of the lens or on the sensor. Around the smear are several small spots. All of this is in the upper right, 3/10 of the way down and 3/10 of the way in from the right side. (I made a JPEG of an image divided into a 10x10 grid. The smear is in the 3rd segment from the top and 3rd from the right.) It is not enough for me to send it back, but it does tell us about the company's quality control.

Guardline 500 Foot Range Wireless Driveway Alarm [4 Motion Detector Alarm Sensors & 1 Receiver] Weatherproof Outdoor Security Alert System for Home & Property Update Sep 2022, 5 years later:
One of the few things that has worked great through rain, sleet, snow, heat and all things Mother Nature can throw at it. Been very happy with this purchase! The sensor finally started having issues 5 years later and found the sensor screen cracked and condensation was getting in. Just bought another one! Highly recommend this product!

Update Sep 2018, 1 year later:
It is located out in the weather and everything has worked great through a year of use in our driveway; very cold winter and very hot summer. I changed batteries recently but did so out of precaution, not because the batteries were weak. We drive in and out at least 4-5 times a day, children ride bikes by it many times a week, along with several trips to the mailbox. About the only thing to watch is when replacing batteries the little screws will fall out if not careful so I placed a white towel underneath since our alarm is mounted on a post with pine straw underneath.
Excellent product and has been great, highly recommend. You can see my full review below.

REVIEW:
After researching several products including much cheaper alternatives, I ultimately decided on this particular brand/model. We use this specifically to alert us of cars coming into our driveway. If you are looking to use this for security reasons, be aware the sensor blinks red when motion is detected which can be seen at night.
Based on two week’s usage, I highly recommend this unit thus far and here is my pros, cons, & discoveries after a few weeks of usage:
Pros/Discoveries:
• Easy to setup and install. Read the manual first!
• Transmitter easily mounts to anything. We used a 4”x4” treated post mounted about 3’6” above the ground. Post is overkill but does look nice.
• Does not seem to have many false alarms but will pick up anything within the range of the sensor which has enough movement to trigger the sensor (as it should). Had one alarm over two weeks that we never saw the reason for the alarm. Perhaps something blew across the sensor. We also have a sprinkler system which sprays water across the sensor and it never alerts, which is good.
• Install the sensor at least 3-4’ above the ground which will avoid most dogs/cats/squirrels, etc., and do not place it on metal. I also would not place it near/within range of bushes/tree limbs or similar items which might move with the wind.
• Adjust the sensitivity distance on the sensor (you must remove the four screws on the sensor to do this). Our driveway is for one car so I decreased the sensitivity level to 23’ (set 39’ from the factory). Options are 13’, 23’, 26’ and 39’.
• You can easily adjust the angle of the sensor once installed.
• Has a sensor low battery indicator which flashes inside on the receiver.
• Easy to add other sensors if needed up to 16 (4 on each zone).
• Uses common batteries. Sensor takes four AA batteries (should last a year); receiver uses four AAA batteries and/or wall outlet power. Receiver can be plugged in with batteries installed acting as a battery backup if power is lost.
• Receiver has plenty of sound melodies to select (~30), and can be very loud if volume is adjusted all the way up.
• No problem with range as our sensor is only about 150’ from the receiver but does go through a couple walls.
• Our sensor is installed in the weather without any other coverings. Based on the instructions it can be mounted anywhere outside and I don’t see the need to put the sensor inside a protective covering.
• I like the removable top of the sensor to keep out weather and sunlight on the sensor.
• The 12 volt relay is a nice option for linking to alarms, gates, or whatever else you might want to do.
• Receiver is easily turned off and on. If leaving home really early on weekends for example, I’ll turn it off to avoid waking my family when I drive out.
• Came with a small screwdriver which fits perfectly to remove tiny screws in the sensor for battery installation and sensitivity setting.

CONS:
• I thought the sensor would have been enclosed in stronger PVC (aka thicker plastic). But it does have a lifetime warranty as long as the company is in business.
• Would have liked more color options for the sensor. For example, black, white and camo.
• Worried about losing the small screws when adjusting sensitivity and/or replacing the batteries in the sensor once installed. Our sensor is installed over a plant bed with pine straw, so I had to put down a white towel under the unit when opening the enclosure to make final sensitivity adjustments. Would have been nice if the sensor came with the type screws that don’t fall out when unscrewed.
• Receiver is not the nicest to look at but we managed to place it where it was centrally located in the house and not so obvious.
• There are over 30 melodies available but we were hoping for more chimes/bells similar to doorbell type options. Many are song type melodies which we didn't like.

Overall very pleased and highly recommend.
I would like to see a wifi enabled version for alerts on a smartphone if desired.
Will update this review should something change.
text_fidelity_b: Guardline 500 Foot Range Wireless Driveway Alarm [4 Motion Detector Alarm Sensors & 1 Receiver] Weatherproof Outdoor Security Alert System for Home & Property

Soundcore by Anker Life P3i Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Earbuds, 4 Mics, AI-Enhanced Calls, 10mm Drivers, Powerful Sound, App for Custom EQ, 36H Playtime, Fast Charging, Transparency, Bluetooth 5.2 I’ve been using the Soundcore by Anker Life P3i Earbuds for about a month. For the price, they are a nice set of earbuds with some good features. The sound quality is above average. I’m not an audiophile; if I can clearly hear Billie Eilish songs, I’m happy.

On the downside, the ANC could be improved and the case itself doesn’t support wireless charging. The earbuds can be charged in the case, but the case itself charges via USB-C.

What I like:
🎧 The earbuds are comfortable. Of course, this is somewhat subjective. But I have a few inner ear piercings (rook, daith, and tragus) and some earbuds irritate my piercings. I can wear this pair for a few hours. And if needed, I can use one earbud at a time, you don’t have to use both for playback.

🎧 The controls are tactile, not touch. I personally dislike touch controls on earbuds, they’re way too easy to accidentally activate. To avoid pressing the earbuds deeper into my ears, I hold onto the “stem” part when using the buttons. The Soundcore app allows customization of the controls, you can change the settings for single tap, double tap, and hold.

What I don’t like:
🎧 The app requires an account to use. Just let me customize my settings without signing up.

🎧 The case can’t be charged wirelessly. It only has one LED status light on the outside. The light only turns red to indicate the case needs to be charged when it has 10% or less remaining.

🎧 The ANC is just okay. I can hear the TV about ten feet away from me.

I have a few work spots in my house, all with cables that slide off the desk. The CordBrick works perfectly to keep those cords in place on the desk. The silicone accommodates all sizes of cords, I’ve even used it with HDMI cables.

I have two complaints. This color is Glow in the Dark, but it doesn’t glow at all! The description actually says it’s “made of a special silicone that has energy absorbing crystals [...].” Apparently, the “energy absorbing crystals” are supposed to suck up any light and use it to make the CordBrick glow. No dice. Mine doesn’t glow at all. So I’m left with a boring, cloudy, off-white colored CordBrick.

The second complaint is very minor: I wish the steel core was fully covered in silicone. One end is visible.

text_fidelity_a:
Cisco-Linksys E4200 Dual-Band Wireless-N Router,Black I bought the Cisco E4200 and the Asus RT-N56U. The RT-N56U was better than the E4200 in strength and speed. Transferring files from laptop to NAS server was much faster with the ASUS both wired and wireless. I however decided to stay with the Cisco because the attached USB hard drive (NTFS) works flawlessly with Windows Backup (not the case with the RT-N56U).

Anyhow, I just switched to AT&T U-verse and tried to have the E4200 get an internet IP address automatically. For some reason it didn't. The ASUS here performed great, as soon as I plugged the cable from AT&T modem/router it configured itself. Amazing! Again... I need those backups in NTFS drives, otherwise I would stick with the RT-N56U.

After trying to troubleshoot myself and losing connection with their chat support, I had to call tech support (in India or surrounding areas). I spent almost hour and a half on the phone, resetting and rebooting everything. The router would just not get an internet IP address. They suggested that the router may be defective, but that I should call AT&T and see if there was something they could do on their end???

Instead of doing that, I drove to my sister house and got her E4200(I did the same setup in her house the week before and it worked well). When I plugged it in, it got the internet IP address immediately, no problems at all.

Both routers had the exact same firmware and settings which indicated to me that the problem was most likely with my E4200.

Again to call Cisco tech support. I explained what happened and told the tech that I had disconnected the router, and that I wanted a replacement. After many questions about how many PCs and laptops I had in my house -irrelevant to the case-, he asked me if there was a cable in lan port one, I replied NO, then he asked the same question about port 2, I replied NO, and so on, until he asked me if there was power going to the router, to which I obviously reply NO. So he said sarcastically 'how do you expect the router to work if it is disconnected?'. I replied 'what part of "I disconnected the router" you did not understand. Misunderstandings like this happened with all the technicians I spoke to.

Another one told me that I had voided my warranty for upgrading the firmware in the router. She scolded me for doing so stating that 3rd party firmware can have bricked the router. I explained to her that I downloaded the firmware from the Cisco support website. She kept going on. I am still trying to figure out where she got the idea that I got 3rd party firmware. What a show of ignorance!

When I asked for a supervisor, they put me on hold for 28 min. After that I was told that there was nobody available. Then the call got mysteriously disconnected when I asked the tech for his full name and badge number.

It is not only Cisco, I know. Many companies do it this way. But it is upsetting that Cisco can not source people who understand and speak English well enough to have a professional conversation. Based on this experience I wonder if these Cisco 'technicians' hold at least a high school diploma.
Yeah, they offer support 24-7-365, but it is not real support if they can not help you or even understand you.

My final advice, if you go for it, test the every single feature of the router. If you find any flaw, deal with Amazon, exchange it or get a refund. Do not try to deal with Cisco-Linksys. It is not worth the aggravation.
text_fidelity_b: Cisco-Linksys E4200 Dual-Band Wireless-N Router,Black

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Chromebook (Wi-Fi, 11.6-Inch) 2012 Model I wanted a computer that was fast and efficient, and didn't bother me with updates all the time. I wanted a device with a keyboard that I could use to surf the Internet, check email, type documents, create to-do lists, update my calendar, and complete quick calculations. I've found all of that and more with Chromebook.

Now, as other reviewers have mentioned, the learning curve might be just a bit steep for those unused to Google's products (besides their search engine, of course). But I'm telling you, once you get the hang of using Google Docs for typing documents, Google slides for creating presentations, Google Calendar for setting dates, etc., you will not want to go back. If you lose your Chromebook or find yourself without it, you can go onto any device that connects to the Internet and find your documents, presentation, calendar, etc.

Technically, you don't even need a Chromebook to use those products, just a Google account. But then you wouldn't have such an efficient, fast machine to use them on--and why would you ever want that?

---------

Just a couple notes on the downsides:

1. Printing is an issue if you don't have a "Cloud Print Ready" printer. Since I don't, my computer scientist husband had to find a work-around.

2. You cannot download external programs. I have to keep my old laptop around for when I want to use iTunes, Blackboard IM (for school), and my scanner. To me, it's no big deal, but don't think that you can use Chromebook for everything because you simply can't. To me, the pros completely outweigh the cons!

Primarily used for a YouTube channel, I started with the mini Flip and Blogger, both had issues with freezing, not to mention low quality. As an incredibly busy and yet lazy person, it was easy.

As cameras got better and cheaper, I went to a snazzy purple JVC Everio, Cyber Shot, and a too complicated Canon Rebel.

Remember that I mentioned laziness?
After all that, I began to use my iPhone, and all the others are collecting dust. No more hours of editing, transferring, formatting, connecting to a laptop, etc.

Even with the external lens, the quality isn't the best, but who cares? I'm lazy!

I started to care, so started to research. This camera has been around for a while. Amazon indicates it was released for sale on its site in 2004, not THAT long of a while, clearly an error. Anyway, the original was re-released WITHOUT a 3G/4G connection in February of this year (2013). Translation...easy-peasy quality at a lower price.

This beauty in gleaming white has the best of all worlds. Choose from thousands on thousands of apps...apps for editing, posting, and more. Over 600,000 droid apps.
If you've used any tablet, any smartphone, this will be like an old friend the first time using it. If you haven't, you'll be amazed at the ease of learning the ins and outs.
Equipped with a good(but not great)lens, large camera/touch display. If you want a tiny camera, get one, but it will have a small display. If you're looking at this, you probably want this size, in every way.

If you do YouTube, Dropbox, etc., it couldn't be easier. Most common apps are preloaded, shoot your video and select via the touchscreen where you want it downloaded.

But even speaking as an iPhone gal, all the great stuff above, when combined with the #1 android device on the market today (the Samsung Galaxy), is pure magic. Talk about a dream marriage!

I went with the protection plan after reading how some people with the previous version had cracked the screen after dropping.

Lazy AND clumsy.

PS...If you have any questions about this camera I may be able to answer, just leave a comment and I'll do my best to help!!!

The voice search works when you want it to and gets out of the way when you don't. Overall, I think we need to see a few more apps for this, such as Crunchyroll, which are undoubtedly on the way. text_fidelity_a:
iPad Stand TechMatte Multi-Angle Aluminum Holder for Tablets, E-Readers and Smartphones, Nintendo Switch - Mini Stand The heft of this stand is impressive. I was expecting a lightweight stand, but was really surprised at how heavy and solid it was when I took it out of the box. It's the type of stand that I get the impression that I could run over with my car and not damage it. The hinge and the "kick stand" portion are made of plastic, but they also feel substantial.

The angle is set by depressing a button in the hinge area. It's very easy to adjust, and the hinge has click stops at various angles that hold it securely.

What is not adjustable is the depth of the cutout that holds the tablet or phone. I didn't have any problems with it holding a variety of tablets (iPad, Kindle and Nexus). It won't, however, hold some tablets that have a skin on it. The cutout that holds the table is slanted, and is 10mm at the widest point at the top, and 8mm at the narrowest point at the bottom. You'll want to measure your tablet plus skin to make sure it fits.

The cutout for the tablet has a plastic non-skid insert that works well. The stand itself also has plastic nubs on the back to prevent scratches on the tablet, and nubs on the bottom to prevent scratches on the table top. The nubs also act as non-skid points.

Very solid build quality, very easy to adjust in a variety of angles, and the design ensures that there won't be any damage to the tablet when you take if off/put it on the stand. As long as the width does not present a problem, this is a great choice for a tablet stand. Highly recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Hosa CMP-105 1/4" TS to 3.5 mm TRS Mono Interconnect Cable, 5 Feet There are many ways one could review this product. I am choosing to give an example of how my family used it. It is a great, functional cable with many other possible uses as well.

After an attempt to use [[ASIN:B005INJ4ZG My Zone Wireless Headphones]] was a bust for me due to its terrible sound quality, my techie husband bought this cable for me as part of a setup that allows me to listen to TV as loud as I want without disturbing him or the neighbors.

I directly hook up this [[ASIN:B000KIPT30 amp]] to a head phone or earbuds when I am sitting close to the TV by using a special [[ASIN:B00009UVPN adapter]]. Head phones and earbuds have a 1/8 inch (3.5 mm) male jack (AKA male connector). Without an adapter, they can't be inserted into this amp, whose plug (AKA socket, female jack, or female connector) measures 1/4 inch (6.35 mm).

Because I like to move around my living room when I am watching TV, my husband also bought me a special [[ASIN:B0010CX798 male-to-female, headphone adapter, extension cable]]. The 1/4-inch, male jack of this cable fits into the 1/4-inch plug of this amp, and it has a 1/8-inch plug on its other end into which the jack of a head phone or ear bud can fit.

In order to use this setup, my husband also hooked into the amp this particular male-to-male extension cable. As you can see, one end is 1/8-inch and the other is 1/4-inch in diameter. The smaller end fits into a plug on the TV. When I want to use this external speaker source, I use the TV remote to access a menu that allows me to do that. Once this system is hooked up, I can no longer adjust the sound volume on the TV itself. I use the volume control on this amp.

Note that there is no On/Off switch on the particular amp we used. If you want to turn it off, so that you are not wasting electricity when it is not in use, you unhook the power cord from the far-left side of the amp.

This setup is a little complicated for the non-techie to figure out on their own, but if you have anyone techie in your family who can do it for you, it works really well.
text_fidelity_b: Hosa CMP-105 1/4" TS to 3.5 mm TRS Mono Interconnect Cable, 5 Feet

text_fidelity_a:
Sony FDRAX53/B 4K HD Video Recording Camcorder (Black) An astonishing example of technology like nothing I've ever seen before.

It's been forty years (!) since I first saw a video camera in high school, a big b/w camera with a backpack that contained the batteries and internals. It was impressive! Then we used a kind of mini-VHS video recorder to share kid videos with our parents maybe 15-20 years ago. Then I got an iPhone which had kind-of video capabilities. So I guess I was ripe to be blown away by this Sony FRAX53/B.

It's small and compact, like a small football. The swing-out screen is breathtakingly crisp and the internal operating system and menus are not only in color, but accompanied by clear, bright sound! I charged the battery and took a video of one of my cats. I could not believe the clarity of the image when I viewed it on the screen! The video is of such high quality that it's easy to overlook the still camera, which is remarkable. High-resolution, bright images. The "Photo" button is kind of oddly placed, it's not easy to operate it while you're holding the device with its right-side hand strap. You can also use a "Manual" mode and twist the lens to achieve custom focus. There's a 20X optical magnification which ought to satisfy anyone.

The Sony software is thorough and functional. The camcorder will transfer photos and video wirelessly if you have a fairly modern computer. I had to use a PC laptop rather than my elderly Mac. That meant using Windows 10, which led to some baffling moments trying to figure out if anything was working.

Between the Sony software and the camcorder and our WiFi setup and Windows 10 I found that the best thing to do sometimes was just WAIT. Windows would give me bad information and I would misinterpret that as an error. Ignore what Windows is telling you and be patient while the FDRAX53/B does its work.

The printed manual is basic and you'll want to spend time reviewing the online documentation. I'm still trying to figure out how to use the Sony FDRAX53/B and a "U-Stream" service to get a live stream going. There is a LOT of technology packed into this camcorder! Expect to spend some time reviewing it all. As I mentioned, Sony packed a TON of features in this device, and there's a learning curve to really understand and appreciate them all.

If you're planning a vacation or expecting a newborn child, BUY THIS CAMCORDER! You cannot take enough videos and photos of your kids when they're young, and the same goes for vacations -- this camcorder is small enough to tote with you (it does not like fog or water, though!) and the QUALITY of the images are incredible! It's not so heavy that it's going to be a burden.

The sound is very good, and there's a "gun" style microphone if you want to A) avoid wind noise B) capture audio of what you're shooting (like at a kid's soccer game) rather than local chitchat.

One thing that occurred to me while I was fiddling with the camcorder in my right hand, that being that if you were holding one of your kids in your left hand and the camcorder in your right hand and they both began to slip... which would you grab? This camcorder is THAT nice. Between the quality of the camcorder and its fantastic lens and the Sony software for image management and manipulation, this could be a major hobby in and of itself. You can easily edit, trim and combine videos with sound and add captions and text. For a consumer level product, the video and image editing suite is quite impressive. You will want a fairly modern computer, as I mentioned.

Something I come back to again and again as I figure the FDRAX53/B out is the absolute wonder of it. The small size, the quality of images, the ease of operation -- I just can't get over it. Beyond sensational and well into the realm of magical. I've never seen anything like the FDRAX53/B before.
text_fidelity_b: Sony FDRAX53/B 4K HD Video Recording Camcorder (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Full Motion Articulating TV Wall Mount Bracket with Swivel and Tilt Features for 32-80 inch TVs and Flat Panels up to 130 Lbs, Black First of all, I'm looking at reviews and pictures of other peoples item and it seems they have a different item, and yet all the reviews are together. Let me start with the good...

PROS_ Inexpensive!

Cons_

THE INSTRUCTIONS: they are written in 6 different languages, and it jumps back and forth between them. It's not broken English, but very hard to follow. Some of them even have a sort of thumbnail of an entire page of text compressed into about 1.5." It is very bizarre. It took about 30 minutes of studying the pictures to figure out what the heck to do, because the manual certainly doesn't tell you. The box comes with sooo much extra hardware to account for different sizes and mounting situations, but the manual does not explain this well.

THE HARDWARE: It is super heavy duty and weighs nearly as much as my TV. My TV is super light weight and is probably 8 or 9 lbs. The bolts that screw into the stud could hold 100lbs I'm sure. Even pre-drilling pilot holes I had difficulty screwing them in with a drill they are so big. It takes so much torque that the screws stripped. I ended up using 1.5" wood screws. I used a stud and I don't like where the TV is mounted, so I am going to get molly bolts to screw it into the drywall where I would like to put it.

NOT STURDY: You mount a plate to the back of the TV, then you mount another piece of hardware to the wall. You then attach the TV to the hardware you just attached to the wall. It is wobbly. It also tilts anywhere from a perfectly neutral position to 20 degree or so angle down. This is in case you are mounting it very high and wish to tilt it down. The TV keeps flopping forward and tilting down. There is a bolt that keeps it in place and I tightened the heck out of it, and it just barely stays put.

NOT FLUSH: I have no other mounting systems to compare it to, but the TV sticks out about 2.5" from the wall. I was expecting it to be much closer.

So there you have it. I am not happy. Ultimately I have the mounted now and no real reason to return it because it's doing what I need it to. There are a lot of positive reviews, but they are I'm sure for a different product. Anyways I paid $15.95. You will most likely be happier with something you pay $25 for.

I included photos of the manual. You can see how the TV mounts, all the extra hardware, as well as a few pages of horrible manual- complete with the mini thumbnail pages.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Full Motion Articulating TV Wall Mount Bracket with Swivel and Tilt Features for 32-80 inch TVs and Flat Panels up to 130 Lbs, Black

text_fidelity_a:
GOgroove Computer Speaker Mini Soundbar - USB Powered PC Sound Bar with Easy Setup Wired AUX, Stereo Audio, Microphone Port, Volume Control Knob, Under Monitor Design for Desktop (Blackout) I bought this as an emergency when my parents' computer speaker went out. Based on the reviews it seemed like it would do the job and it seemed simple which is all we needed.

The connections are very simple and its a good looking speaker. Ideal for placing in that little space beneath a monitor in front of the stand. The headphone jack and manual volume dial is also a nice touch.

So everything up to the point of unboxing and connecting was great. Then we turned on the sound. It is tinny, there was no bass or even midrange body, and there was tons of distortion even at a modest volume. The best way I could characterize it is an old AM clock radio with a single speaker from the 70s. There wasn't anyway I could push decent volume out of these speakers and I tried every combination of source and speaker volume I could figure. If I was trying to use this on a laptop I wouldn't even bother. Better off with a cheap pair of computer speakers from Walmart.

Giving it two stars really because it does work, it had nice features, and it plays sound for very little money. But if you want better sound than what comes out of a cheap radio, spend a little more and get a lot more out of it. I can't imagine this speaker being useful in any way.
text_fidelity_b: GOgroove Computer Speaker Mini Soundbar - USB Powered PC Sound Bar with Easy Setup Wired AUX, Stereo Audio, Microphone Port, Volume Control Knob, Under Monitor Design for Desktop (Blackout)

text_fidelity_a:
Magellan Crossover 3.5-Inch Portable GPS Navigator OK, so I can't compare the performance of this GPS system to any other as this was the first time I've ever used or needed something like this. But I read a lot of reviews, and I do mean a lot of them, for a couple of weeks before making my decision and I'm pleased that for a first experience I purchased a Magellan Crossover.

Let me explain, I work in sales. I travel to a lot of large towns/ small cities in my territory that are in Arkansas. I had never been to these towns before. Apparently, the city leaders do not care if one can find their way around them because most of them have terrible city maps available and/or do not bother to put street signs up. This made it a challenge to find my customers even with a map.

So the idea of a GPS came to mind and I took the plunge. This little unit worked exactly the way I wanted for 2 days then stopped working half way through the second day. Not even pressing the reset button helped. (sigh) I called the people I purchased it from and they paid to have it Fed-Exed back to them for replacement. Apparently I got a defective model. Hey, it happens to all of us. So by the end of this week I'll have my replacement and will be ready to roll again.

This was a great time saver for me. I would get to a town, input the first address and it would get me to my first stop. When I was done there I would input the next address and it accurately got me to the next place I needed to be. It literally saved me a couple hours a day in wasted travel time by my not having to stop, get directions from a local (that were usually wrong) and repeating that process over and over.

The screen was bright and easy to read, the voice plenty loud enough. And the unit was easy learn to use. I gave it 5 stars for performance. I can't really fault the manufacturer for a faulty unit. Those things are hard to predict and usually are few and far between.

So, unless the next unit is also defective, at which time I will then have to reconsider and write a more negative review LOL, this little GPS unit is a great buy for a first time user.

[...].
text_fidelity_b: Magellan Crossover 3.5-Inch Portable GPS Navigator

One day it just stopped charging. I had read dozens of books on there, and had the wifi plus 3g version which was very convenient.

I occasionally read now on the Kindle app on my computer, as I have about 97 books in my library, with probably 15-20 still unread. I noticed on Amazon that there was a promotion...Kindles on sale for Prime members. I thought, you know, it would be nice to read those books I've put off reading because it's just not the same on my computer or phone...I think I'll get another Kindle. I researched reviews for a little while, and decided all I needed was the Paperwhite with Wi-fi. The additional cost for 3G was just not worth it to me...sure, I'd used it before when traveling with my old Kindle to buy a few books, but with a little planning I could've purchased and downloaded the books beforehand. Also, some of the reviews of the higher end Kindles did not impress me.

Anyway, I received the Kindle earlier today. It came almost fully charged, and was so easy to set up. And within minutes had books from my Kindle library loaded! I've been reading for 2 hours straight and so far I love it. I am using it on maximum brightness, sure it may take more frequent charging, but I really love how bright it is and the contrast of the words on the page. I also bought a cover for it and find it is easier to hold IMO. Pages turned with a simple finger swipe.

Hopefully this will last a very long time! I've got so many books I want to read!

HP Wireless Elite Keyboard v2 ...if you don't have a wrist rest or pad already, I highly recommend that you get one at the same time you get this keyboard. I was introduced to the chiclet- or scissor-style keyboard because of using one at work (using an Apple wired keyboard with an Intel Mac), and I have to say that I prefer it in every way to the more traditional keyboards. It is much quieter, and, for me, the feedback is pleasant. One thing I did not take into account, though, is that I had a wrist rest at work. So when I got this keyboard for home use and started using it, I loved it immediately--until the day I used it for hours on end. Then--ouch! My wrists began to ache.

Overall, this is a great keyboard. It connected to my computer without a problem, and the only lag in keystrokes I have experienced has been when the computer had just been "awakened" from sleep mode. For reasons I will not go into here, I am using this keyboard with a laptop: the laptop keyboard's lights indicate whether or not I have Caps Lock or Num Lock engaged on the wireless keyboard. I understand that won't help people using this keyboard with a desktop computer, but thought I'd put it out there anyway.

My conclusion: if you're a fan of the scissor-style keyboard and you have or are willing to invest in a wrist rest, you will enjoy this keyboard.
text_fidelity_b: HP Wireless Elite Keyboard v2

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech MX Keys Mini Minimalist Wireless Illuminated Keyboard, Compact, Bluetooth, Backlit, USB-C, Compatible with Apple macOS, iOS, Windows, Linux, Android, Metal Build - Graphite I’ve been using the Logitech MX Keys Mini for about two weeks now. I like it, but I don’t love it. The keyboard won’t replace my current favored mechanical keyboard, I love linear switches too much, but it has some uses.

The typing experience is decent. The keyboard is at a fixed angle, it cannot be adjusted. The bottom of the keyboard does have rubber “feet” so that it doesn’t slide around. No movement on my desk mat or plain desktop. The keys have what Logitech calls a “spherical dish” which looks like a little cup on the top of each key. My fingers naturally settle in the indentation but it’s not something I notice when typing.

The keyboard isn’t silent, but it’s much, much quieter than a mechanical keyboard. There’s a little tactile feedback, so I do feel the keypresses, which I like.

The form factor of the keyboard is, well, mini. The size makes it a good solution if you don’t have a lot of space on your desk or want to take it on the go. Logitech made some sacrifices with keys, but did keep the arrow keys. Whew. If you need a numpad, this isn’t the keyboard for you.

I really wish the backlighting could be controlled via the keyboard. The brightness can be adjusted, but that’s it. Otherwise, the keyboard is “smart” enough to know when you are typing and illuminate, but when your hands aren’t on it, or you stop typing for a few seconds, the backlighting turns off. When I’m using my computer in the dark, reading an article or watching something, it’s really annoying to have the backlighting flicker in and out.

The backlighting and other customization options are set in Logi Options, Logitech’s software. I already use Logi Options for my MX Master 3 mouse, but try as I might, I could not get the software to recognize the keyboard. I have to use High Sierra for a program I rely on, and after going through a bunch of suggested troubleshooting, I think that’s why. So if you’re like me and using an older version of macOS, you might have trouble getting the keyboard recognized by Logi Options. Because of this, I can’t use Flow, either.

The MX Keys Mini can connect with up to 3 devices at once, the first three function keys allow quick switching between devices. I tried to pair my MacBookPro and Note20 Ultra to test this, and was able to easily pair both and switch. The keyboard ONLY connects to devices via Bluetooth or the Logi Bolt USB Receiver (which isn’t included). A USB-A to USB-C cable is included for charging only. Because I can’t get Logi Options to recognize the keyboard, I can’t check battery life and know when it needs to be charged.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech MX Keys Mini Minimalist Wireless Illuminated Keyboard, Compact, Bluetooth, Backlit, USB-C, Compatible with Apple macOS, iOS, Windows, Linux, Android, Metal Build - Graphite

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Show - 1st Generation Black If there were a way to give this negative stars I'd do it. Amazon, seriously. I don't understand you guys. Half the time you do great things and the other half the time I frankly at am a loss for words. Do you do ANY testing at all before you go to market? Seriously, who decided this was ready to be sold as is.

Me: Alexa show my videos
Echo: Here are your photos.

Me: Alexa show me my movies.
Echo: here are your videos. ( I asked for videos and got photos. I have for movies and it gives me my videos. )
but then it only shows me about 20 of my more than 100 movie Library.

Me: Alexa, show me a calendar
Echo: here is what's on the calendar. (no, I want to see a calendar month for this month)
I tried everything. There is no calendar. If I wanted to see events, I'd ask to see events. See how that is logical? I want to see a calendar. It's not rocket science. It's that basic thing that hangs on everyone's wall? You know a 30 day calendar?

So I begin to think maybe this isn't my account...

Me: Alexa, who's account is this.
Echo: This device has only one account, Alex's.
A last name would be good here. Lot's of Alex's out there.

Me: Alex's show me what's on prime video
Echo: YouTube plays something I have no idea what it is.

I can't ask what's on prime video. It has no concept of what I am asking. And this just goes on and on. Stick with me Amazon. I have an idea. You have a video based Echo. Maybe, just maybe, it would be a good idea that we could ask this video based echo what new movies are on prime video?? Yah think? I eventually got it to show me some prime movies. It seems to pick 20 to show as a selection. Kind of like when it showed me a selection of 20 of my movie library even though I have well over a hundred.

Me: Alexa, show songs from my library.
Echo: this shows 50 random songs from my library.

Me: Alexa, show albums in my library.
Echo: this shows 50 albums. Better than the response I got from my movies query.

Here are some request to make this living disaster better.

Me: Alexa, show me my video collection.
This should result in showing me movies and tv shows I own and/or have rented. I should be able to choose movies from here.
once in movies, I should be able to search for a movie by name from this point.

Me: Alexa, show me a calendar.
This should result in showing me a calendar for the current month, with Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun across the top and all the numbers of the weeks below. I ought to be able to then say, what's going on for the 14th. And it should be the 14th. I should be able to say, add event for the 14th and then add the event. I know, rocket science, right?

Me: Alexa, show me holidays for this month.
The result, I think you know...

If I ask to see my shopping list it says I have one item "1 Song" if I ask it to show me 1 or song or both it fails to understand what I am talking about.

Bottom line, this is JUST NOT FINISHED. Not by a country mile. You have to be kidding me if you think this is ready for the end user.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Show - 1st Generation Black

text_fidelity_a:
Sony HDR-PJ380/W High Definition Handycam Camcorder with 3.0-Inch LCD (White) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) While I'm quite comfortable using an SLR, I've not been all that handy with a camcorder in the past. It's been a few years since I used one, so I was curious to see if user-friendliness has kept pace with technological advancements.

With this model it has. I found it very easy to use right out of the box with just some minor trial and error. I did end up reading the manual (which is pretty decent) but the main functions were pretty self apparent by just fiddling around with it a bit. The menu structure is logical and well presented; the screen is clear and easy to view.

The overall build quality is excellent. It feels more substantial in hand than I expected at this price point while retaining a very lightweight and easy to carry profile. I like the button placement - feels very natural in hand.

I love having the internal memory for storage as well as the little touches, such as a built-in USB connector. These features help make this a grab-and-go type of device, which increases the likelihood and ease of bringing it along and capturing video. (Note: you can also use a plug-in memory card should you want to.)

The video quality in good light/outdoors is excellent - very sharp and clear. Low-light performance is a somewhat grainy but quite decent. Stills are pretty decent. It won't put an SLR to shame, but it's more than good enough for casual snapshots. The internal mic works well and is more immune to wind noise than I expected.

My only significant disappointment with the cam is the projector. Wonderful idea, but the actual performance is lackluster. The projected video is hard to see clearly if there's any appreciable amount of light in the room. The 100 inch projection spec is wildly optimistic if you expect to actually see what is being projected.

Given that this cam does everything else so well, is so easy to use, and a breeze to tote along, I won't detract any stars due to the shortcomings of the projector feature. This is a great cam for the novice cam user (such as myself) or even an intermediate user. However, if the projection feature is a primary need, this may not be a good cam for your needs.
text_fidelity_b: Sony HDR-PJ380/W High Definition Handycam Camcorder with 3.0-Inch LCD (White) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

USB Power Strip Portable Travel Charger Outlets 2.1AMP 1AMP 21W 5Foot Power Supply Cord With Universal Plug Input From 100v-240v Power Sockets USB Charger Station 4 Port 5v 1A/2.1A USB Charger (White) This is a very unique and awesome product. It wasn't listed near the beginning of my Amazon search results, so it took me a while to find it. But it's AWESOME!!!

The first thing I do when I get to a hotel room or a cruise ship cabin is to set up my charging station. We have phones, iWatches, Kindle, iPad, and rechargable power packs, so we end up having a lot of potential things to charge. Setting up the charging area is a high priority. The best place is on a table or desk, so we can spread out our rat's nest of cables and devices with easy access. However, power outlets are often in inconvenient places, especially on a cruise ship. (On cruises, in the past I would actually bring a small extension cord.)

Anyway, this super clever travel charger solves the problem. I can plug it into the wall outlet, and run the cord up onto a table or desk. It's perfect.

Actually, the 4 USB ports isn't nearly enough for us, so one of these chargers wasn't going to entirely solve my problem. Theoretically, I could use two of them, but that's overkill in the sense that I don't need long two cords. Since this charger has a wall-plug type of outlet on the charger itself, I already have regular wall power at the charger on the table. I don't need to run a second cord from a wall outlet. Therefore, I use a small 4-port USB charger without the cord, and plug that into this charger. That gives me 8 USB ports up on the table for easy access. Here's the 4-port charger without a cord that I plug into this one:
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07JH9R89T/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o01_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

I have never seen a charger with a cord like this before, and I am very impressed with how clever and useful the design is! The one problem I found was with the child protection piece inside the slots on the charger's power socket. (This is the 110V power socket on the charger.) Because of the child protection piece, it can sometimes be very hard to get something plugged into that socket. The protection piece needs to slide to the side, so you can't just push the plug straight in, like you would at a wall socket. You need to put the prongs into the slots at an angle, and pry the protection piece out of the way. It's a pain. So, if you don't need the child protection, and you intend to use that socket, you'll probably want to remove the protection piece.

Here's how to do that. The top surface is a snap-off cover. Pull it up in the middle of one of the side, and slip a little screwdriver in there to carefully pry around and pop it off. Then there's a second cover inside that isn't attached, and will almost just fall out. On the back of that second cover, you'll see the two little springs and the plastic protection piece. Pull out the springs and the protection piece, and then put it all back together.

[NOTE: Do not remove the child protection if there will be children near it, or if you have any other safety concerns about its removal. Remove it at your own discretion and your own risk. I'm not telling you to remove it. I'm just telling you how to remove it if you want to.]

Anyway, I actually went a step further. The socket seems to be designed to accept any plug in the universe, so there are a lot of extra holes and spaces (i.e. it's not just two little slits for the normal US plug). I took white electrical tape, and taped over all the extra holes and spaces on the secondary (internal) cover, leaving just the two slits open. Then after popping on the outer cover, you just see the two open slits. All the other openings are covered internally with the white electrical tape. I think it looks much better, but this is purely a cosmetic step.

At first, it seemed like the clip for the plug is on the wrong side. It's on the same side as the USB ports. If you leave the plug in the clip (and leave the cord wrapped around the charger), then rotate the plug down 90 degrees, you can plug it into a wall outlet and the charger would be flush against the wall, hanging down from the wall socket. That seemed like it should be a nice neat way of using it without extending the cord, if desired. However, you can't do that because the USB ports end up against the wall, and you can't access them. If the clip was on the opposite side, it would work fine. As it currently is, in order to use it, you need to flip it around so the USB ports are facing out. But since the plug clip is on the wrong side, the charger sticks out from the wall at an angle. At first this seemed like a design flaw. Then I read in the instructions where it specifically says you shouldn't do any charging while the cord is wrapped around it. Presumably that's a heat issue. Therefore, it is probably designed this way on purpose, to discourage you from attempting to use the charger with the cord wrapped around it.

The bottom line is that there is no design flaw. It's prefect just the way it is. And you need to unwrap the cord when you use it, which is fine with me, since having the cord extended is the best feature of this charger.

Anyway, I think this is an awesome little gadget.
text_fidelity_b: USB Power Strip Portable Travel Charger Outlets 2.1AMP 1AMP 21W 5Foot Power Supply Cord With Universal Plug Input From 100v-240v Power Sockets USB Charger Station 4 Port 5v 1A/2.1A USB Charger (White)

text_fidelity_a:
Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th) The Fire HD 10 tablet is pretty much an unbeatable deal for a tablet these days. You get a really good display and decent processor and memory for a great price---especially when it's on sale. And the Fire OS (a rebranded and modified version of Android) works smoothly.

A trade-off is a not-so-good camera resolution.

And there are some limitations on what you can do. If you already own some Android apps, you might not find them in the Amazon app store, and those you do will not credited as paid for. You'll have to buy them again (if you choose to buy).

One option is to follow online instructions for installing the Google Play Store on your Fire. But that's kind of iffy. You don't know when the next Fire OS update might break that installation. And Play Store might download updates to some of the core Fire OS apps that might conflict with proprietary Fire OS modifications.

Another consideration is that this device serves as an advertising and sales platform for Amazon. It's tailored for that. Something to keep in mind.

The thing to consider is if you can be happy with what Amazon gives you. If you're going to be trying to root and work around the OS and app store limitations soon after you get it, maybe it's worth just getting an Android tablet and foregoing the Fire.

If you can be happy with all that, overall it's a great deal for a capable tablet.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th)

text_fidelity_a: Transcend USB 3.1 SDHC/SDXC/ microSDHC/SDXC Card Reader, TS-RDF5R (Pink) First, I need to clear up why I am only giving this four, instead of five, stars:  the cap covering the USB connection doesn't fit onto the back of the unit.  That irritates me because the cap will inevitably disappear, leaving the USB end permanently uncovered, even when in storage.  Otherwise, this unit completely rocks ~ I purchased it to transfer data via USB 3.0 onto/from micro SDXC cards, and it does that both fabulously and quickly.  I moved 16GB from a 32GB card in just a couple of minutes (literally, a couple of minutes, not twenty+) on my Windows 8.1 machine.  There's no way I could have transferred the same data so quickly using my high-res music player, which isn't USB 3.0.  Note that you cannot read from both an SD and micro SD card at the same time on this unit; you can only read from one or the other.  I also like that there is a blue light on the card reader that comes on when it is ready.  The blue light will go off if you insert a second card into the unit concurrently with another, letting you know that the unit is not ready.  If you want a reliable little reader, this is for you, if you're not bothered by the cap issue.
text_fidelity_b: Transcend USB 3.1 SDHC/SDXC/ microSDHC/SDXC Card Reader, TS-RDF5R (Pink)

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG Galaxy S9+ Factory Unlocked Smartphone 64GB - Midnight Black Samsung does not care about customer satisfaction. For them customer-centric culture is a very foreign idea. This is my experience. I will never buy Samsung electronic device again and will convince all my friends and family to avoid that trainwreck also.

Bought this phone new in July 2018, at Best Buy. Phone started to act up couple months later, not taking up the charge, finally turning into a brick. And since then it was a road through hell of Samsung (questionable) quality and dealing with the worst customer service I have ever encountered... It is unbelievable, because I expected Samsung to be on par with Apple, but boy, am I disappointed!

So - it has essentially been the following cycle: would not take charge -- repair (2 weeks) - would take charge for a day, then would not take charge - - repair (2 weeks) - would take charge for a day, then would not take charge - - repair (2 weeks) - would take charge for a day, then would not take charge - then I finally decided to call customer service again, but demanding refund, being fed up with this whole brand altogether. It's been quite a ride with those guys, too! It took them first a few days to reply, oh sorry, I take it back - to do nothing, then I called last Friday (12/07) demanding refund again. Then I was told 48 hrs for decision. Then nothing, so I called Wednesday, after 72 hours and was escalated to someone else who told me it is up to five days, so I need to wait until Friday 12/14 (today) and they'd call me with the decision. So I waited till Friday's late afternoon because - of course - nobody called, and after being elevated again, spending about 2 hr and demanding information, I was told the phone cannot be refunded, not even exchanged! Only repaired again (because they have policies that say that main board has to be replaced). Next week I was supposed to get this phone on an international trip. Now I am stranded without one, I just haven't got some $700's around to buy new phones anytime I feel for it.

It is unbelievable that they have some unrealistic policies and it does not matter that phone breaks 4 times (the same thing) and they would not replace it, let alone refund it, cause "it wasn't motherboard". My communications with even 2nd level manager was just as that - pointless. Banging my head against the wall of some corporate baloney - rather than being cared about as a customer who does genuinely get hit by their product poor quality.

GO FOR iPHONE INSTEAD!!! Maybe the phones aren't Androids but at least they have some true customer service out there!
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG Galaxy S9+ Factory Unlocked Smartphone 64GB - Midnight Black

text_fidelity_a: SanDisk 256GB Ultra Dual Drive USB Type-C - USB-C, USB 3.1 - SDDDC2-256G-G46 I use this to transfer files in a multi-platform (Macs & PCs) environment. Having both the standard USB interface and the newer USB-C interface in the same thumb drive is very handy. The device is fairly compact considering the two connectors are both recessed for travel. It gets a bit warm during heavy transfer activity, but not enough to be a problem. The only reason I didn’t give 5 stars is because it is fairly slow for large files. And, by large files we’re talking anything over 2GBs, so not that large. Moving 10-15 GBs takes several minutes. I also have an older version of this device and it was just as slow. Therefore, I’d say even though they have upgraded the product standard to USB 3.1, it appears to be the same chip as the older version and the chip is the limiting factor. If you need a multi-platform capable thumb drive, this is a worthwhile purchase. But don’t expect fast transfer speeds.
